{{nihongo|'''Amatsu Shrine'''|天津神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Echigo Province]].

'''Amatsu Shrine''' (あまつじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Ichinomiya, {{ill|Itoigawa|ar|إتويغاوا (نييغاتا)|azb|ایتوییقاوا، نیقاتا|ce|Итоигава|ceb|Itoigawa (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Itoigawa|es|Itoigawa|fa|ایتویی‌گاوا، نیگاتا|fi|Itoigawa|fr|Itoigawa|gl|Itoigawa|id|Itoigawa, Niigata|it|Itoigawa|ja|糸魚川市|ko|이토이가와시|mg|Itoigawa|ms|Itoigawa, Niigata|mzn|ایتویی‌گاوا، نیگاتا|nl|Itoigawa|pl|Itoigawa|pt|Itoigawa|ro|Itoigawa|ru|Итоигава|sv|Itoigawa|tg|Итоигава|tl|Itoigawa, Niigata|tr|Itoigawa|tt|Итоигава|uk|Ітоїґава|ur|ایٹوئیگاوا|uz|Itoigava|vi|Itoigawa, Niigata|war|Itoigawa, Niigata|zh|糸魚川市|zh_classical|絲魚川市|zh_min_nan|Itoigawa-chhī|zh_yue|絲魚川|qid=Q857208}}, {{ill|Niigata Prefecture|Q132705|qid=Q132705}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|ja|論社|qid=Q135022904}} and claims the status of {{ill|Ichinomiya|ca|Ichinomiya (Xinto)|de|Ichi-no-miya|fr|Ichi-no-miya|id|Ichinomiya|ja|一宮|ko|이치노미야|pt|Ichinomiya (templo)|simple|Ichinomiya|th|อิจิโนมิยะ|uk|Ітіномія (титул)|zh|一宮|qid=Q1656379}} of {{ill|Echigo Province|be|Этыго (правінцыя)|ckb|پارێزگای ئێچیگۆ|cs|Provincie Ečigo|de|Provinz Echigo|es|Provincia de Echigo|fa|ولایت اچیگو|fr|Province d'Echigo|gl|Provincia de Echigo|id|Provinsi Echigo|it|Echigo|ja|越後国|ko|에치고국|lt|Ečigo žemė|nl|Echigo (provincie)|pt|Província de Echigo|ru|Этиго (провинция)|simple|Echigo Province|sk|Ečigo (provincia)|sr|Провинција Ечиго|tr|Echigo (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Етіґо|zh|越後國|zh_min_nan|Etigo-kok|zh_yue|越後國|qid=Q666514}}. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine ranking system}}, it was classified as a {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=prefectural shrine|qid=Q90139226}}.

=== Overview ===
It is traditionally said to have been founded during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|Q329723|qid=Q329723}}, and is also said to have been an imperial prayer shrine (chokuganjo) of {{ill|Emperor Kōtoku|ar|الإمبراطور كوتوكو|arz|الامبراطور كوتوكو|azb|کوتوکو (ایمپیراتور)|be|Імператар Котаку|ca|Kōtoku Tennō|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر کۆتۆکو|cs|Kótoku|de|Kōtoku|es|Kōtoku Tennō|fa|امپراتور کوتوکو|fr|Kōtoku|id|Kaisar Kōtoku|it|Kōtoku|ja|孝徳天皇|ka|კოტოკუ|ko|고토쿠 천황|mr|कोतोकू|nl|Kotoku|pl|Kōtoku|pt|Kotoku|ru|Император Котоку|sh|Car Kōtoku|simple|Emperor Kōtoku|sl|Cesar Kotoku|sv|Kotoku|th|จักรพรรดิโคโตกุ|tl|Emperador Kōtoku|tr|Kōtoku (imparator)|uk|Імператор Котоку|uz|Imperator Kōtoku|vi|Thiên hoàng Kōtoku|wuu|孝德天皇|yo|Emperor Kōtoku|zh|孝德天皇|zh_min_nan|Kôtoku Thian-hông|zh_yue|孝德天皇|qid=Q317980}}. Revered as the {{ill|Ubusunagami|Q1392097|qid=Q1392097}} (tutelary deity) of areas including Ichinomiya, Oshiage, Teramachi, Ōmachi, and Shichikenmachi within the former which was changed to red-seal land the following year. In Taishō 7 ({{ill|1918|Q2094|qid=Q2094}}) it was ranked as a village shrine, and later promoted to a prefectural shrine.

In the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'', a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} named “{{ill|Echigo Province|be|Этыго (правінцыя)|ckb|پارێزگای ئێچیگۆ|cs|Provincie Ečigo|de|Provinz Echigo|es|Provincia de Echigo|fa|ولایت اچیگو|fr|Province d'Echigo|gl|Provincia de Echigo|id|Provinsi Echigo|it|Echigo|ja|越後国|ko|에치고국|lt|Ečigo žemė|nl|Echigo (provincie)|pt|Província de Echigo|ru|Этиго (провинция)|simple|Echigo Province|sk|Ečigo (provincia)|sr|Провинција Ечиго|tr|Echigo (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Етіґо|zh|越後國|zh_min_nan|Etigo-kok|zh_yue|越後國|qid=Q666514}} {{ill|Kubiki district|ja|頸城郡|qid=Q11664982}} Ōjinja” is listed, and this shrine is considered a candidate site ({{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|ja|論社|qid=Q135022904}}) for that entry. In addition, the subordinate Nunagawa Shrine within the precincts is also a disputed Shikinaisha.

=== Auxiliary and branch shrines ===
[[File:Amatsu-jinja (Itoigawa), Nunagawa-jinja.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Nunagawa Shrine}}]]
* Nunagawa Shrine
*: The principal enshrined deity is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nunakawa-hime-no-Mikoto}}, later joined by Yachimata-no-Mikoto ({{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944}}). This area was formerly called “Numakawa-gō,” and {{ill|Japanese mythology|Q814158|qid=Q814158}} (the {{ill|Myth of Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主の神話|zh|大國主之神話|qid=Q11433656}}) recounts that Yachimata-no-Mikoto visited Nunakawa-hime-no-Mikoto, who lived there. According to tradition, the child born to these two deities was {{ill|Takeminakata|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto|qid=Q9150391}}, who traveled upstream along the {{ill|Hime River|arz|نهر هيميكاوا|fa|رود هیمه|fr|Hime-gawa|ja|姫川|ru|Химекава|qid=Q11447417}} into {{ill|Shinano Province|ckb|پارێزگای شینانۆ|cs|Provincie Šinano|de|Provinz Shinano|eo|Provinco Ŝinano|es|Provincia de Shinano|fa|ولایت شینانو|fr|Province de Shinano|gl|Provincia de Shinano|hak|Shinano-koet|id|Provinsi Shinano|it|Shinano (provincia)|ja|信濃国|knc|Shinano Province|ko|시나노국|lt|Šinano žemė|ms|Wilayah Shinano|nl|Shinano (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Shinano|pt|Província de Shinano|ru|Синано (провинция)|simple|Shinano Province|sk|Šinano (provincia)|sr|Провинција Шинано|th|แคว้นชินาโนะ|tr|Shinano (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сінано|zh|信濃國|zh_min_nan|Sinano-kok|zh_yue|信濃國|qid=Q289250}} and developed the land there.
*: In the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'', it is listed as one of 13 shrines in {{ill|Kubiki district|ja|頸城郡|qid=Q11664982}}. There are several shrines named “Nunagawa Shrine” within the district besides this one; the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nunagawa Shrine}} in Tabushi Minami-mura, Itoigawa City (former village shrine), and the {{ill|Nō Hakusan Shrine|Q11611996|qid=Q11611996|lt=Hakusan Shrine}} in Ōaza Nōmiyaue, Itoigawa City (former village shrine), are also considered disputed sites for the Shikinaisha Nunagawa Shrine.
<gallery>
File:Amatsu-jinja (Itoigawa), keidaisha.jpg|Shrine within the precincts
</gallery>

=== Festivals ===
Among its festivals, bugaku (court dance) is well known ({{ill|Tenshin Shrine Kagura|Q11442800|qid=Q11442800}}). Commonly called “Chigo no Mai” (Dance of the Sacred Children), it is dedicated during the April annual festival.

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property (National designation) ===
* Itoigawa and Nō Bugaku — encompassing the {{ill|Tenshin Shrine Kagura|Q11442800|qid=Q11442800}} of Itoigawa and the {{ill|Hakusan Shrine Bugaku|Q11579603|qid=Q11579603}} of Nō. Designated on January 28, 1980 (Shōwa 55).<ref>{{National Cultural Properties Database|302|53|Itoigawa and Nō Bugaku}}<br/>{{National Cultural Properties Database|312|312|Amatsu Shrine Bugaku}}</ref>

=== Niigata Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties ===
* Tangible Cultural Properties
** Wooden statue of Nunakawa-hime (sculpture) — Late Heian period. Designated February 10, 1954 (Shōwa 29).<ref name="Niigata Prefecture Cultural Properties">{{PDFlink|[https://www.pref.niigata.lg.jp/uploaded/attachment/130374.pdf List of Cultural Properties of Niigata Prefecture]}} (Niigata Prefecture website).</ref>
** Bugaku masks (3 pieces; with 2 additional bugaku masks and 3 chigo dance masks) (sculpture) — Late Kamakura period to late Muromachi period. Designated March 27, 1981 (Shōwa 56).<ref name="Niigata Prefecture Cultural Properties"/>
** Wooden seated statues of goddesses (3 figures) (sculpture) — Heian period to Kamakura period. Designated March 27, 1981 (Shōwa 56).<ref name="Niigata Prefecture Cultural Properties"/>

=== Itoigawa City Designated Cultural Properties ===
* Tangible Cultural Properties
** Main hall of Amatsu Shrine (structure) — Designated March 26, 1991 (Heisei 3).<ref name="List">{{PDFlink|[List of Designated and Registered Cultural Properties]}} (Itoigawa City website).</ref>
** Wooden statues of guardian deities of Amatsu Shrine (2 figures) (sculpture) — Designated March 25, 1972 (Shōwa 47).<ref name="List"/>
** Wooden statues of guardian deities of Nunakawa Shrine (2 figures) (sculpture) — Designated March 25, 1972 (Shōwa 47).<ref name="List"/>
** Stone seated statue in the form of a Tathāgata (sculpture) — Designated April 22, 1980 (Shōwa 55).<ref name="List"/>
** Amatsu Shrine large hanging Buddhas (2 pieces) (crafts) — Designated March 26, 1973 (Shōwa 48).<ref name="List"/>
